status.description: "ok" for a normal round. "blocked" only when the manuscript cannot be made to build at all: the loop then stops instead of spending the remaining budget writing into a tree that does not compile. Required, so that leaving the tree buildable is a statement the result makes rather than a field it can omit.

build_blocker.description: Required with status "blocked": the file, the error, and why it cannot be fixed from here.

compiles.description: Whether the brief's compile command succeeded on the manuscript as you left it. Must be true unless the result declares status "blocked"; the contract enforces this.

compile_command.description: Verbatim from brief.json; reported with its outcome.

numbers_used.description: Every numeral introduced this round, with the file it came from. A number without a source is a fabrication.

placeholders_used.description: The brief's placeholder ids whose macro this round wrote into the manuscript, e.g. ["ph-prod-speedup"]. A placeholder site is not a number: emit \ph{<id>} and report the id here, and never put a value at that site. paper-audit matches this list against the sites actually present in the text, so a site written without being reported is the same class of defect as an unreported numeral — and a number written at a registered site is worse than either.

structure.description: What the structural pass changed, or 'skipped: <reason>'.

reason.description: The missing evidence, not a lack of time.

storyline_deviations.description: Where the prose departs from the confirmed plan. Silent departure is the defect this field exists to catch.

x-piano-assertions.message: compiles must be true: a stage may not finish with a manuscript that does not build. Fix the build, or report status "blocked" with a build_blocker naming the file and the error.
status "blocked" asserts that the manuscript cannot be built, so a blocked result must report compiles: false. A spurious block stops the loop and spends the rest of the budget doing nothing.

qc.voice: Replaced a 'In order to' opener with the reference spec's consequence-first form; removed two instances of 'leverage' from the banned list.
